Toy list of missing taxa

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_missing_taxa_list.Rd

Valid missing_taxa_list for phylograftR::toy_backbone, with 7 taxa to graft by phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa().

It is the output of phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() applied to the table system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa.csv", package = "phylograftR"): open that file to see how to fill the table. It shows target clades defined by one or two tips, excluded subclades (named or not, with one tip or several), and the stem settings. Clades and excluded subclades are named after the taxonomic groups of phylograftR::toy_backbone_taxonomic_table (e.g., "Family_A").

Usage

data(toy_missing_taxa_list)

Format

A named list with 7 taxa and the following items. Every item is named after the taxa ($Taxon_name), in the same order.

  • $Taxon_name Character vector. Names of the taxa to graft.

  • $Target_clade List of character vectors of tips defining the target clade of each taxon (one tip: the terminal branch of this tip).

  • $Target_clade_name Character vector. Labels of the target clades. Not used for the grafting, but checked against the names of total_richness_per_clades, if provided.

  • $include_target_clade_stem Logical vector. Whether the stem of the target clade of each taxon is available for grafting (NA uses the global argument).

  • $Excluded_subclades List (one element per taxon) of named lists of character vectors of tips defining the excluded subclades, or NULL.

  • $exclude_subclades_stem List (one element per taxon) of logical vectors (one value per excluded subclade), or NULL.

See phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() for the use of the items in the grafting.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_backbone for the backbone phylogeny.

  • phylograftR::toy_total_richness_per_clades for the total richness of the target clades.

  • phylograftR::toy_taxonomic_tables for the taxonomic tables of the backbone and of the missing taxa.

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to import such a list from an external table.

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() to build such a list from a data.frame.

Examples

# Import the list from loaded datasets
data(toy_missing_taxa_list)
str(toy_missing_taxa_list, max.level = 1)
#> List of 6
#>  $ Taxon_name               : chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Target_clade             :List of 7
#>  $ Target_clade_name        : Named chr [1:7] "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_B" ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ include_target_clade_stem: Named logi [1:7] TRUE TRUE FALSE NA TRUE NA ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Excluded_subclades       :List of 7
#>  $ exclude_subclades_stem   :List of 7

# Compare to the initial '.csv' file
system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa.csv", package = "phylograftR")
#> [1] "/home/runner/.cache/R/renv/library/phylograftR-802cedf8/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/phylograftR/extdata/toy_missing_taxa.csv"
